frequency_question: How often does institutional regulatory friction successfully block or prevent the implementation of a proposed macroprudential capital buffer increase within a designated two-year window?
membership_rule: Includes any formal proposal or active staff-level consideration of raising the CCyB or systemic risk capital buffers by US banking regulators; excludes microprudential institution-specific enforcement actions.

cases.name: Federal Reserve review leaving CCyB at 0% (2018)
Federal Reserve review leaving CCyB at 0% (2019)

provenance_note: 4 cases named, 10 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (2.5x)
coverage_note: 4 named relevant macroprudential review cycles; universe of annual reviews spans 2016 to 2026.
known_gaps: Internal Federal Reserve staff memos are not systematically tracked until public release.
skeleton: Regulatory review cycles for the CCyB conducted annually since establishment, where institutional friction (inter-agency disagreement, comment period delays, and economic model calibration disputes) prevents moving above 0%.
multiplier: 4 review cycles with active friction outcomes out of 10 total annual review opportunities since 2016
validity_reason: Regulatory frameworks and voting structures at the Federal Reserve Board of Governors remain stable over this horizon.
